title: Developments in Cryomicroscopy: Automated Sample Preparation and Optical Cryofluorescence Imaging Boost Performance in Cryo-EM
content:
Abstract
Sample preparation for cryomicroscopy, and especially correlative light and electron microscopy, is difficult due to several areas that affect sample integrity and orientation. Here we review various standard cryomicroscopy sample preparation techniques and provide details on the CryoGenium, a new blot-free cryo-EM sample preparation system comprised of two compartments: a humidity compartment where the sample is applied to a grid by dipping, and a cryo-compartment in which the sample is vitrified via plunging into a temperature-controlled cryogen bath. The humidity compartment provides a stable environment allowing users to control the sample temperature, humidity dewpoint, and film thickness. In this compartment, the sample grid can be viewed with an optical microscope, allowing researchers to monitor the interaction between the grid and liquid, and to adjust liquid film thickness in real time to determine the optimal moment to trigger vitrification in the cryo-compartment.
